Hi Lena/Vanessa —

Quick first-cut technical sizing notes (assumptions called out). Please treat as an ops estimate; we'll refine after we confirm model dims and real token distributions.

Assumptions: AURI-70B ~ 70B params, KV key/value dims = 16k (hidden size), 32k max context. We use 16-bit tokens for activations in FP16 baseline.

1) KV cache memory (per concurrent prompt)
- KV entries scale linearly with context. Rough rule: KV_memory_bytes ~ context_length * hidden_dim * 2 (bytes per FP16) * 2 (key+value)
- For 32k context: 32_000 * 16_384 * 2 * 2 ≈ 2.097e9 bytes ≈ 2.1 GB per concurrent session
- For 8k context: ~0.525 GB per concurrent session

2) Concurrent sessions and effective pool sizing
- Assistant workload: target steady QPS 15 with avg generation ~600 tokens. Effective concurrency depends on latency; with p95 target 450ms we expect concurrency ~15 * 0.45 ≈ 6.7 concurrent requests. Apply 2x headroom for spikes => 14 concurrent contexts => KV cache footprint ~14 * 2.1 GB ≈ 29.4 GB just for KV cache
- Scoring workload: 60 QPS with 150 tokens and p95 1.2s => concurrency ~72 (60 * 1.2) but smaller context 8k. Headroom 1.5x => ~108 concurrent => KV cache ~108 * 0.525 GB ≈ 56.7 GB

3) Model memory + activation working set per GPU
- A 70B model FP16 (~2 bytes/param) ~140 GB; with sharded inference kernels this can be split across 4–8 GPUs depending on tensor-slicing strategy.
- Activation working set and beam/kv overhead add another 10–30% depending on sequence lengths and kernel choices.

4) Quantization impact (practical numbers)
- INT8/quantized kernels reduce model weight storage ~2x–2.5x vs FP16 (so 70B weights ~60–70 GB in INT8 packed format), but KV cache and activations typically remain FP16/bfloat unless we enable mixed-precision KV caching.
- If we keep KV in FP16: KV cache savings from weight quantization do not reduce KV footprint; however total GPU memory required per replica can drop 20–35% enabling denser packing or fewer GPUs per shard.
- Aggressive KV quantization (FP16 → INT8) can further reduce KV footprint ~2x, but risks small accuracy regressions; for R&D assistant workloads we recommend a staged evaluation: pilot with model weight INT8 + FP16 KV, then evaluate INT8 KV on a holdout prompt set.

5) Suggested pool config (first pass)
- Reserved pool: 6 x A100-80GB (or equivalent) for model shards + 1.5x buffer for activations and KV. With INT8 weights (server-side) we can consolidate to 4–5 GPUs but leave buffer for rolling upgrades.
- Separate scoring pool: 8 x H100-80GB (or equivalent) with faster infer kernels and CPU-backed batching; scoring benefits from more replicas with smaller contexts to keep latency predictable.

Attachments: aurigene-sizing-v1.xlsx (workbook with calculations and scenario tabs)

Thanks Marcus — extremely helpful. Lena, for procurement framing we typically show two commercial options:

Option A — 12-month reserved pool (lowest $/token):
- Commitment: monthly GPU reserved units to cover the reserved pool outlined above
- Benefit: guaranteed headroom, preferred latency SLA (p95 targets), lower unit cost; 60-day termination with winddown for enterprise

Option B — 3-month pilot + burst credits (faster start):
- Commitment: pilot credits to run 1–2 shards (for microbench) + burstable hosted API for peak experiments
- Benefit: lower upfront, flexibility to validate INT8 KV before committing; higher $/token when bursting

Commercial ask: can you sign an MSA + pilot addendum so we can start the microbenchmarking? Once Marcus verifies INT8+FP16 KV throughput we will produce a finalized capacity + pricing proposal. I'll attach the two commercial templates after this thread (DocuSign link).
